# Wicket Oat Support

This skill helps you build modern Wicket applications using the Oat UI library.

## Quick Start

### 1. Installation
In `WebApplication.init()`:
```java
WicketOats.install(this);
```

### 2. Base Layout
Extend `OatAppLayout` for your main pages to get the sidebar and topnav structure, or `OatMobileLayout` for a phone-first app with a bottom tab bar (`OatBottomNav`). For the signed-in user's menu in the top bar, return an `OatUserMenu` from `newTopNavExtra(id)`: picture or initials and name, a menu with your links and "Sign out", or a "Sign in" link while nobody is signed in.

### 3. Creating UI
Oat components are plain Wicket components, created with `new`; those driven by a callback have a static factory taking a lambda, like Wicket's `AjaxLink.onClick(...)`:
```java
// A component
add(new OatAlert("saved", "Your changes were saved.", OatVariant.SUCCESS));

// A button, without an anonymous subclass
add(OatButton.onClick("id", "Label", target -> { ... }));

// A behavior on an existing component
myLabel.add(Oat.Behaviors.badge(OatVariant.SUCCESS));
```

## Components and Behaviors

- **Components** (`new OatAlert(...)`, `OatButton.onClick(...)`): standard UI widgets with encapsulated markup.
- **Behaviors** (`Oat.Behaviors`): Oat styling for *any* standard Wicket component, for custom logic and deep customization.

## Layout and Styling: Oat CSS Only

Wicket Oat uses Oat's CSS and nothing else. Never add Tailwind, Bootstrap or other utility classes. Prefer plain semantic HTML (Oat styles `form`, `fieldset`, `header`, `footer`, `nav`, `table`, `dialog`, ... directly), and use only Oat's built-in utility classes for layout:

- Stacks: `vstack`, `hstack`
- Flexbox: `flex`, `flex-col`, `items-center`, `justify-center`, `justify-between`, `justify-end`
- Spacing: `gap-1`, `gap-2`, `gap-4`, `gap-6`, `mt-2`/`4`/`6`/`8`, `mb-2`/`4`/`6`/`8`, `p-4`, `w-100`
- Text: `align-left`, `align-center`, `align-right`, `text-light`, `text-lighter`
- Lists and links: `unstyled`
- From `wicket-oat.css`: `oat-divider` (a line with a word in the middle, e.g. `<div class="oat-divider">or</div>`); `<kbd>` is styled as a key
- Grid: `container`, `row`, `col-1`...`col-12`, `offset-1`...`offset-6` (or `Oat.Behaviors.row()`/`col(6)`/`container()` from Java)

No other sizes exist (no `gap-3`, `mt-5`, `px-4`, ...). For anything else, write a small CSS rule in the application's own stylesheet using Oat's CSS variables (`var(--space-4)`, `var(--primary)`, ...).

## Reference Material

- [COMPONENTS.md](references/components.md): Full list of available components and form fields.
- [BEHAVIORS.md](references/behaviors.md): Detailed guide on styling via composition.
- [THEMING.md](references/theming.md): How to switch and define themes.

## Common Tasks

### Form Handling
Oat form fields work like plain Wicket form components: with a `CompoundPropertyModel` on the form, leave out the model (it is inherited by id) and the label (looked up by id in the `.properties` file).
```java
Form<MyData> form = new Form<>("form", new CompoundPropertyModel<>(data));
form.add(new OatTextField<String>("name").setRequired(true)); // MyPage.properties: name=Name
form.add(OatSubmitButton.onSubmit("save", "Save", target -> ...));
// After an Ajax submit the fields show (and clear) their errors themselves: no target.add(form) needed
```
For the form's own messages next to it, e.g. `form.error("...")`, add `form.add(new OatFeedbackPanel("formFeedback", form))`; page-wide feedback and toasts then leave them out.

### Toasts & Notifications
Prefer Wicket's own feedback messages and let Oat display them - as toasts with `add(Oat.Behaviors.feedbackToasts())` on the (base) page, or as alerts with `add(new OatFeedbackPanel("feedback"))`. Both update during Ajax requests on their own:
```java
success("Saved."); // in any event handler; no target.add(...) needed
```
For a one-off toast with a title, call the `Oat` facade directly:
```java
Oat.toast(target, "Message", OatVariant.SUCCESS, "Title");
```

---

Source: https://github.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/blob/v0.6.0/wicket-oat/references/components.md

# Wicket Oat Components

Oat components are plain Wicket components: create them with `new`. Those driven by a callback (`OatButton`, `OatSubmitButton`, `OatAccordion`, `OatTabs`, `OatDropdown`, `OatButtonGroup`, `OatBreadcrumb`, `OatPagination`, `OatAvatarGroup`, `OatWizard`, `OatLoginForm`, `OatLazyLoadPanel`) also have a static factory taking a lambda instead of a subclass, like Wicket's `AjaxLink.onClick(...)`, listed below; `Oat.Components` has the same factories under one roof (`Oat.Components.button(...)`, `accordion(...)`, ...).

## Variants
Colors are a single `dev.jbaby.wicket.oat.OatVariant` enum everywhere (alerts, badges, buttons, toasts): `DEFAULT`, `SECONDARY`, `SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `DANGER`. Buttons style `SECONDARY`/`DANGER`; badges all; alerts and toasts `SUCCESS`/`WARNING`/`DANGER`. There are no per-component `Variant` enums.

## General
- `new OatAlert(id, message?, variant?)`: Creates an `OatAlert`. `message`/`variant` can each be a plain value, an `IModel`, or omitted.
- `new OatBadge(id, label, variant?)`: Creates an `OatBadge`. `label` can be a `String` or an `IModel<?>`.
- `OatButton.onClick(id, label, onClick)`: Creates an `OatButton` with an Ajax click handler, on an `<a>` or `<button>`. The label is rendered as the tag's text, so the markup is just `<a wicket:id="save"></a>` (no inner `<span wicket:id="label">` - that now fails). `new OatButton(id) { onClick... }` without a label renders the markup body instead, e.g. an icon with `setIcon(true)`.
- `new OatSplitButton(id, label, onClick)`: `OatSplitButton`, a button for the usual action joined to a "▾" button with a menu of related ones (Oat's `menu.buttons`). `addAction(label, target -> ...)` returns the entry for `.setVariant(OatVariant.DANGER)`; `setVariant`/`setStyle`/`setSize` apply to both buttons. The "▾" button is named by the `OatSplitButton.more` resource ("More actions").
- `OatSubmitButton.onSubmit(id, label, onSubmit, onError?)`: Creates an `OatSubmitButton`, an Oat-styled `AjaxButton` that submits its form: `onSubmit` runs when the form is valid, `onError` when it isn't (e.g. `target -> form.error("Please fix the errors.")`); Oat fields show their own errors without it. Markup: `<button wicket:id="save"></button>`. Subclass `OatSubmitButton` directly to override `onSubmit`/`onError` instead.
- For slow actions, `setBusyIndicator(true)` on either button (off by default) shows a spinner (`aria-busy`) while its Ajax request runs and ignores further clicks, so the action can't run twice. `OatDialog.setBusyIndicator(true)` does it for the dialog's confirm button, and `Oat.Behaviors.ajaxBusy()` for other Ajax links and buttons.
- `new OatCard(id)`: Creates an `OatCard` container.
- `new OatAvatar(id, urlModel)` / `new OatAvatar(id, initials)` / `OatAvatar.initials(id, initialsModel)`: Creates an `OatAvatar` from just an image URL or just initials. Note `new OatAvatar(id, model)` takes a picture URL, not initials.
- `new OatAvatar(id, urlModel, initialsModel, size)`: Creates an `OatAvatar` with a picture over initials, which show while it loads and if it can't be loaded (Wicket Oat's script hides a failed picture); `size` is required in this overload. The models are read once on every render; a blank URL is no picture. `OatAvatar.initialsOf("Ada Lovelace")` gives `"AL"`.
- `OatAvatarGroup.of(id, model, size?, populateItem)`: Creates an `OatAvatarGroup` (a clustered/overlapping set of avatars).
- `new OatEmptyState(id, title, message?)`: Creates an `OatEmptyState` placeholder.

## Layout & Navigation
- `OatAccordion.of(id, model, exclusive?, populateItem)`: Creates an `OatAccordion`.
- `OatButtonGroup.of(id, model, populateItem)`: Creates an `OatButtonGroup` container for buttons.
- `OatBreadcrumb.of(id, model, populateItem)`: Creates an `OatBreadcrumb` trail, a panel on `<nav wicket:id="...">` (with nothing inside: it brings its own markup) named by the `OatBreadcrumb.label` resource ("Breadcrumb"; `setLabel(...)` or an `aria-label` in the markup for another name). Not shown without levels. `populateItem` adds each level's `link` with a `label` child; the last is marked `aria-current="page"`, or `setCurrent(titleModel)` ends the trail with the current page as text. `setMaxItems(n)` (at least 2, counting the current page) leaves levels out of a longer trail: the first, a "…" button (`OatBreadcrumb.more`, "Show more levels") whose menu has the levels in between (populated the same way, as `role="menuitem"` links), and the last ones. The levels are read once per request; each list item's id and model index is the level's index among all of them (`breadcrumb:list:tail:4:link`).
- `new OatPagingNavigator(id, pageable)` / `new OatAjaxPagingNavigator(id, pageable)`: `OatPagingNavigator` / `OatAjaxPagingNavigator`, Wicket's (Ajax)`PagingNavigator` rendered as Oat pagination for any `IPageable` (`DataView`, `PageableListView`, `DataTable`). Prefer these whenever there is an `IPageable`. For the Ajax one, the pageable or a parent needs `setOutputMarkupId(true)`. For a `DataTable` of your own, `table.addBottomToolbar(new OatNavigationToolbar(table))` and `table.addTopToolbar(new OatHeadersToolbar<>(table, provider))` (in `components.table`) give it `OatDataTable`'s Ajax paging row and `aria-sort` headers.
- `OatPagination.of(id, model, populateItem)`: Creates an `OatPagination` control - hand-rolled page links for when there's no `IPageable`; you style the current page yourself. The `<nav>` is named by `OatPagination.label` ("Pagination"), unless its markup has an `aria-label`.
- `OatDropdown.of(id, triggerLabel, model, label, onClick)`: Creates an `OatDropdown` popover menu whose items show `label.apply(item)` and run `onClick(target, item)` over Ajax when chosen; the menu then closes.
- `OatDropdown.of(id, triggerLabel, model, populateItem)`: The same with items you populate yourself (each is a `<button role="menuitem">` with a `"label"` child); call `dropdown.close(target)` after handling a click.
- `new OatTabbedPanel<>(id, tabs)`: Creates an `OatTabbedPanel`, Wicket's `AjaxTabbedPanel` with Oat styling. Tabs are `ITab`s - build them with `Oat.tab("Title", SomePanel::new)` (the factory receives the panel id). Only the selected tab's panel is created, and switching swaps it over Ajax; `new OatTabbedPanel<>(id, tabs, selectedIndexModel)` keeps the selection in your own model. Prefer this for panels that are expensive or need server state.
- `OatTabs.of(id, model, populateTab, populatePanel)`: Creates an `OatTabs` tab strip + panels, all rendered up front and switched in the browser by the `ot-tabs` web component.
- `new OatDialog(id, header)` / `new OatDialog(id, triggerLabel, header)`: Creates an `OatDialog` modal on the native `<dialog>` element. It works like Wicket's `ModalDialog`: set the content with `setContent(component)` - the component must use the id `OatDialog.CONTENT_ID` - and open and close it from any Ajax handler with `dialog.open(target)` / `dialog.close(target)` (`open` re-renders it first); `open(content, target)` sets content that is removed again on close. With a trigger label it also renders a button that opens it in the browser. The server tracks `isOpen()`: Cancel, Escape and a click on the backdrop close it in the browser and tell the server, the overridable `onClose(target)` runs once whenever it closes (also after a confirm or `close`), and `target.add(dialog)` keeps an open dialog open. The content sits in the dialog's own form, so fields in it are validated when Confirm is clicked: on a validation error the dialog stays open and shows them inline; otherwise the overridable `onConfirm(target)` runs and the dialog closes unless an error was reported in it there (e.g. `field.getInput().error("Taken")`) or it was opened again there (e.g. for the next record). Put it on a tag of its own (`<div wicket:id="dialog"></div>`, no box of its own) so `target.add(dialog)` works; on `<wicket:container>`, which deployment mode strips, only `open`/`close` do. Inside a page's form its buttons render as `type="button"` (`NestedFormButtonBehavior`, also on `OatSubmitButton`), so Enter in a page field can't click them. `OatConfirmDialog` ignores Confirm clicks while an answer is handled. `setConfirmLabel`, `setCancelLabel` and `setConfirmVariant(OatVariant.DANGER)` customize the buttons; the default labels come from the `OatDialog.confirm` / `OatDialog.cancel` resource keys. `setCloseButton(true)` adds an "×" in the header's corner (named `OatDialog.close`; first in the markup, and wicket-oat.js focuses the first field on opening), and `setFooterVisible(false)` leaves out the footer with Cancel and Confirm (Enter in a field then submits nothing). The content scrolls between header and footer. Closed in the browser, the dialog's fields show the models again next time (input not confirmed and errors are dropped; the server is told once the dialog is out of sight). An open dialog rendered again shows without animating in again. `getDialogElement()` is the `<dialog>`, for a subclass.
- `new OatDrawer(id, header)` / `new OatDrawer(id, triggerLabel, header)`: `OatDrawer`, an `OatDialog` (same API: `setContent`, `open`/`close`, `onConfirm`/`onClose`, Cancel/Confirm) that slides in from an edge as a side panel, for filters, a record's details or an edit form: `setSide(OatDrawer.Side.END)` (default; as tall as the screen, `min(24rem, 100% - 3rem)` wide), `START`, or `BOTTOM` (as wide as the screen, up to 85% of its height); start and end follow the text direction. It has the "×" by default; the content scrolls between header and footer, which stays at the bottom. For a drawer that only shows something, `setFooterVisible(false)`. Its setters return `OatDrawer`, so they chain with `setSide`.
- `new OatPageHeader(id, title)`: `OatPageHeader`, a `Border` on a `<header>`: breadcrumb, title (`<h1>`, looked up by id when no title is given) and subtitle on one side, and the tag's own content as the actions on the other (wrapping below on narrow screens). `setSubtitle(...)`, `setBreadcrumb(List<MenuItem> | IModel<List<MenuItem>>)` - links to the pages above, ending with the title as the current page (`aria-current`), in a `<nav>` named as any `OatBreadcrumb`; it is one, and `setBreadcrumbMaxItems(n)` leaves levels of a long one out.
- `new OatPopover(id, triggerLabel, id -> content)`: `OatPopover`, a button opening a panel with any content (an `ot-dropdown` with a popover), e.g. a filter or quick-edit form; the factory must use the id it is given (`OatPopover.CONTENT_ID`). `close(target)`, `getContent()` to re-render it, `getTrigger()`.
- `OatWizard.onFinish(id, target -> onFinish)` / `new OatWizard(id) { onFinish(target) }`: a form over several steps with numbered steps (`aria-current="step"`; finished steps are links back). `addStep(title, id -> component)` - created when the step is shown, so keep data in a shared object; it is rendered on a `<div>`. Next validates the step's fields inline (Enter does the same; Finish on the last step); Back and step numbers go back without validating. Override `onNext(step, target)` and report an error on a component to keep the user on a step. `getCurrentStep()`/`setCurrentStep(i)`. Texts: `OatWizard.back`/`.next`/`.finish`, step list named by `OatWizard.steps`.
- `OatLoginForm.signIn(id, (user, pass) -> boolean)` / `new OatLoginForm(id) { signIn(user, pass, rememberMe) }`: username (`autocomplete="username"`), password (`current-password`), Sign in (busy). A failed attempt shows `OatLoginForm.failed` without saying which part was wrong and clears the password; a successful one gives the session a new id (`changeSessionId()`, keeping its metadata) and calls `onSignedIn(target)` (default: `continueToOriginalDestination()`, then the home page). `setRememberMe(true)` shows the checkbox, `setForgotPasswordLink(PageClass)` a link. The core doesn't depend on `wicket-auth-roles`; call e.g. `AuthenticatedWebSession.get().signIn(...)` in `signIn`.
- `new OatCrud<>(id, columns, provider, rowsPerPage)`: `OatCrud<T, S>`, an `OatDataTable` plus "New" (with `setNewItem(Supplier)`), Edit and Delete in an actions column, an edit `OatDialog` and an `OatConfirmDialog`. `setEditor((id, model) -> panel)`: the panel gets a `CompoundPropertyModel` over the record (pass it to `super(id, model)`; Oat fields named after properties bind by themselves). `setOnSave((target, record) -> ...)` runs after a valid save (report an error on a field to keep the dialog open), `setOnDelete(...)` after confirming; `setTitle(Record::name)` names it in "Edit {0}" / "Delete {0}?"; `setSearch(id -> component)` beside "New" (its Ajax handler re-renders just the rows: `target.add(crud.getDataTable().getTable())`); `getDataTable()`, `create(target)`, `edit(target, record)`. Edits load the record via `provider.model(...)`. Texts `OatCrud.*`.
- `new OatTree<>(id, ITreeProvider)`: `OatTree<T>` (`components.tree`), Wicket's `NestedTree` styled with Oat (`.oat-tree`, no theme images). `setLabel(fn)`, `setIcon(node -> iconName)`, `setOnSelect((target, node) -> ...)` (labels become links, `aria-current` on the selected one; `select(target, node)`). Expand buttons are `<button>`s with `aria-expanded` and `OatTree.expand`/`collapse` labels ("Expand {0}"). Nodes are compared by the provider's models (`equals`).
- `new OatTableTree<>(id, columns, ITreeProvider, rowsPerPage)`: `OatTableTree<T, S>`, a tree grid (Wicket's `TableTree`); put a `new TreeColumn<>(Model.of("Name"))` among the columns, other columns as in a data table. Oat headers (`aria-sort` with an `ISortableTreeProvider`), paging, `OatTableTree.empty`; `setLabel`, `setIcon`, `onSelect`. Focus returns to a node's button after toggling.
- `new OatMenuBar(id)`: `OatMenuBar`, a row of small ghost buttons (`setStyle(ButtonBehavior.Style)` to change). `addAction(label, target -> ...)`, `addLink(label, PageClass[, params])` (it has `aria-current` while that page is shown), `addMenu(label)` returns a `Menu` with `addAction(label, ...)` / `addAction(IModel label, OatVariant.DANGER, ...)`. Put it on a `<nav aria-label="...">`.
- `new OatSplitLayout(id, id -> first, id -> second)`: `OatSplitLayout`, two panes, each scrolling on its own. The first is resizable with the browser's own corner handle (CSS `resize`, no JS). `setSplit(20..80 in steps of 10)` sets its starting share; `setOrientation(VERTICAL)` stacks them (28rem high by default). Below 768px they are stacked and not resizable. The factories must use the ids they are given (`first`, `second`).
- `new OatMasterDetail<>(id, selectionModel)`: `OatMasterDetail<T>`, a list beside the selected item's details. `setMaster(id -> component)` (any component; it calls `select(target, item)` and can use `isSelected(item)`), `setDetail((id, itemModel) -> component)`; an empty state (`OatMasterDetail.empty`) while none is selected. Below 768px one shows at a time, with a Back button (`OatMasterDetail.back`, `showList(target)`); switching keeps the list's scroll position.
- `new OatConfirmDialog(id)`: `OatConfirmDialog`, an `OatDialog` that asks before an action runs. Add one per page and call `confirm.ask(target, header, message, t -> action)` from any Ajax handler (`String` or `IModel<String>` texts; `message` may be `null`); the action runs on Confirm, at most once, and Cancel/Escape closes without running it. One dialog serves any number of buttons. The confirm button is `DANGER` by default; `setConfirmLabel`, `setCancelLabel`, `setConfirmVariant`, `setHeader` and `setBusyIndicator` return `OatConfirmDialog`, so they chain with `ask`.
- `OatAppLayout`: (Base Page) Provides sidebar and topnav, and applies the current theme. Subclasses pass `PageParameters` (or a model) to `super(...)`; override `sidebarMenuItemsModel()` to return `MenuItem`s - `MenuItem.of(label, PageClass)` or `MenuItem.of(label, PageClass, pageParameters)`, with a `String` or `IModel<String>` (e.g. `ResourceModel`) label. `MenuItem.group(label, items...)` makes a collapsible section of links (open while one of its pages is shown; groups can't be nested), and `item.withBadge(IModel<?> | String)` adds a badge after a link's label, read on every render and hidden while `null`, empty or zero (e.g. `withBadge(() -> orders.countOpen())`). The sidebar has a markup id, so `target.add(getSidebar())` re-renders it, e.g. to update badges. Items for pages the user isn't authorized to instantiate are left out (and a group left empty), and an item is active when the page class (and its parameters, if any) match. It sets `lang` on `<html>` from the page's locale and starts with a "Skip to content" link (`OatAppLayout.skipToContent`) to `<main id="oat-main">`, shown only while focused. The title, name and menu-button label default to the `OatAppLayout.title` / `OatAppLayout.name` / `OatAppLayout.toggleMenu` resources; override `appTitleModel()`/`appNameModel()`, `newTopNavExtra(id)`, `newSidebarFooter(id)` and `newMenuLink(id, item)` (e.g. an `AjaxLink` instead of the default `BookmarkablePageLink`) to customize.
- `new OatBottomNav(id, List<BottomNavItem>)` / `new OatBottomNav(id, IModel<List<BottomNavItem>>)`: a tab bar fixed to the bottom of a phone's screen, on a `<nav>` (named "Main" by `OatBottomNav.label`; `setLabel(...)` or an `aria-label` in the markup to change it). Three to five tabs, each an icon above a short label: `BottomNavItem.of(label, PageClass[, params])` with `withIcon(Icon.sprite("symbol-id") | Icon.svg("<svg>...</svg>") | Icon.named("calendar"))` - a symbol of the page's own SVG sprite (`<svg><use href="#id"/></svg>`), trusted inline SVG (not escaped: never user input), or an `OatIcon` name; draw sprites and SVGs with `currentColor`. `withBadge(() -> count)` shows a count on the icon, hidden while `null` or 0. `asPrimary()` makes one item the bar's main action, a round Oat `a.button` (`button oat-fab`) showing only its icon (the label becomes `aria-label`; it needs an icon) and never colored as the current tab. The current tab gets `aria-current="page"` (same page class, and parameters if the item has any); `withActive(page -> ...)` replaces that rule, e.g. `page -> page instanceof TeamPage || page instanceof MemberPage`. Tabs for pages the user isn't authorized to instantiate are left out. Hidden above 768px unless `setAlwaysVisible(true)`. Override `newLink(id, item)` to return another `AbstractLink` (e.g. an `AjaxLink`). Its rules are in `wicket-oat.css`; content under it needs `padding-block-end: calc(var(--oat-bottom-nav-height) + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))`, and the viewport meta tag needs `viewport-fit=cover` for the iPhone's safe area.
- `new OatUserMenu(id, nameModel)`: `OatUserMenu`, the signed-in user's menu for `OatAppLayout#newTopNavExtra`: picture (`setPicture(urlModel)`) or initials and name on a button named "Account: <name>" (picture only on phones), opening their name, `setDetail(model)` (e.g. email), `addLink(label, PageClass[, params]).setIcon("settings")` links (the current page's marked `aria-current`) and "Sign out". The name model returns `null` while nobody is signed in; then it shows a "Sign in" link to `setSignInPage(PageClass)` (hidden on that page), or nothing. "Sign out" (a POST from a stateless form, which also works after the session expired; refused with 403 when the browser's `Sec-Fetch-Site` says another site's page sent it) calls `signOut()` (default: `getSession().invalidate()`, which takes effect at the end of the request) and `onSignedOut()` (default: home page; go to a page with `setResponsePage(PageClass)`); override them, e.g. for Spring Security. Override `isSignedIn()` for a signed-in user without a name. The models are read once per request. Keeps pages stateless; has a markup id for `target.add(userMenu)` after an Ajax sign-in. Texts: `OatUserMenu.account`/`signIn`/`signOut`.
- `OatMobileLayout`: (Base Page) a phone-first page: the content in `<main class="oat-mobile-main">`, as wide as the bar's tabs (`--oat-bottom-nav-max-width`, 28rem) with room below, and an `OatBottomNav` after it. Override the abstract `bottomNavItemsModel()`; `newBottomNav(id, items)` to customize the bar (e.g. `setAlwaysVisible(true)`); the `bottomNav` field has a markup id for `target.add(getBottomNav())`. Applies the theme, density and `lang` like `OatAppLayout`, and its viewport meta tag has `viewport-fit=cover`.

## Form Components
- `new OatMultiSelectField<>(id, label, IModel<List<T>>)`: `OatMultiSelectField<T>`, an `OatCustomField` with chips (remove buttons named `OatMultiSelectField.remove`) and a search box (Wicket's `AutoCompleteTextField`): `setChoices(text -> list)`, `setDisplay(fn)`, `setMaxChoices(n)`. Choosing adds the value and clears the box; chosen ones aren't suggested again. Required means at least one. Chips added or removed are like typed input: they reach the model on submit, and `form.clearInput()` drops them (`OatDialog` does that on open and cancel), so one dialog can be reused per record. Works inside an `OatDialog`/`OatPopover`, like `OatAutoCompleteField`: `wicket-oat.js` shows Wicket's suggestion list above them (Escape closes the list, then the dialog).
Form fields are `Oat[Type]Field` classes in `dev.jbaby.wicket.oat.components.form` (`OatTextField`, `OatEmailField`, ...), except `OatTextArea`, `OatDropdownChoice`, `OatCheckBox`, `OatSwitch`, `OatFileUpload`, `OatFileDropzone` and `OatTagInput`.

Every one takes an optional trailing hint-text model — but only when `label` is passed as an `IModel<String>`, not a plain `String`:
`new Oat[Type]Field(id, IModel<String> labelModel, model, hintModel?)`. There is no `(id, String label, model, hintModel)` overload; wrap the label in `Model.of("Label")` if you need a hint.

The label and the model can also be left out, exactly like plain Wicket form components: `new Oat[Type]Field(id)` inherits the model from a parent `CompoundPropertyModel` by id, and `new Oat[Type]Field(id, model)` keeps an explicit model. A missing label is looked up in the `.properties` files with the id as the key (falling back to the id). `OatDropdownChoice` mirrors `DropDownChoice`: `(id, choices, renderer?)` and `(id, model, choices, renderer?)`.

Behavior of the field panels:
- Required fields get `aria-required="true"` and an asterisk after their label (via `data-required` on the field container). The native `required` attribute is deliberately not set, since the browser would block the submit with its own message before Wicket could show its inline error.
- After an Ajax request that validates them (e.g. a submit) they show an error that appeared, changed or went away by themselves, without `target.add(...)`: they update their message and error state in place, so the input keeps its focus and what the user typed. Other Ajax requests leave the errors shown alone. They also render their own tag with a markup id, so `target.add(field)` (or `target.add(form)`) re-renders them. Attributes on that tag in your markup (e.g. `class`) are kept.
- The wrapped `FormComponent` is the field's child `input` (`BaseOatField.INPUT_ID`), so in a `FormTester` its path is `"<fieldId>:input"` (e.g. `formTester.setValue("email:input", ...)`), and `getInput()` returns it, e.g. for `setNullValid(true)` or `new EqualPasswordInputValidator(password.getInput(), repeat.getInput())`.
- `field.add(...)` sends validators and `AjaxFormComponentUpdatingBehavior`s (including `OnChangeAjaxBehavior` and `AjaxFormChoiceComponentUpdatingBehavior`) to the input; other behaviors apply to the panel's own tag. `addToInput(...)` adds any behavior to the input, e.g. `addToInput(AttributeModifier.replace("autocomplete", "email"))`. Subclasses create the input in `newInput(id, model)`.
- Single-input fields (text, password, email, number, URL, search, tel, date, date-time, time, month, week, money, percent) take `setSuggestions(List<String> | IModel<List<?>>)` - values the browser suggests as the user types, from a native `<datalist>` (anything else can still be typed) - and `setPrefix(text)`/`setSuffix(text)` (a `String` or `IModel<String>`; `null` hides it): text addons such as `https://`, `kg` or `€` in Oat's input group. Without one the field renders as usual.
- Fluent setters (`setRequired`, `setLabel`, `setPlaceholder`, `addValidator`, `add`, and `setMin`/`setMax` on number/range fields) return the concrete field type, so they chain freely.

- `new OatTextField<>(id, label, model)`
- `new OatPasswordField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatEmailField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatNumberField<>(id, label, model)`
- `new OatTextArea<>(id, label, model)`
- `new OatDropdownChoice<>(id, label, model, choices, renderer?)`
- `new OatRadioChoice<>(id, label, model, choices, renderer?)`: `OatRadioChoice`, radio buttons in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`; stacked, or in a row with `setInline(true)`. Same constructor/factory shapes as `dropdownChoice`.
- `new OatCheckBoxMultipleChoice<>(id, label, model, choices, renderer?)`: `OatCheckBoxMultipleChoice`, a checkbox group bound to an `IModel<? extends Collection<T>>` of the selected choices (updated in place); `setInline(true)` for a row.
- `new OatListMultipleChoice<>(id, label, model, choices, renderer?)`: `OatListMultipleChoice`, a `<select multiple>` bound to a collection of the selected choices; `setMaxRows(n)` sets its height.
- `new OatCheckBox(id, label, model)`
- `new OatSwitch(id, label, model)`
- `new OatRatingField(id, label, IModel<Integer> model)`: `OatRatingField`, stars to choose a rating from (radio buttons with values `"1"`..`"5"` in a `<fieldset>` with a `<legend>`, each named "3 stars" by `OatRatingField.stars`); hovering previews, the arrow keys move between stars. The model holds the number of stars, `null` while none is chosen; `setMax(1..10)`. Test: `formTester.setValue("rating:input", "4")`.
- `new OatDateField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatDateTimeLocalField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatTimeField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatColorField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatUrlField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatSearchField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatTelField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatMonthField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatWeekField(id, label, model)`
- `new OatRangeField<>(id, label, model)`
- `new OatFileUpload(id, label, model)`
- `new OatFileDropzone(id, label, model)`: Drag-and-drop alternative to `OatFileUpload`.
- `new OatMoneyField(id, label, model)`: `OatMoneyField`, an amount bound to a `BigDecimal`, shown and parsed in the user's locale (`1.234,50` / `1,234.50`, `inputmode="decimal"`). `setCurrency(Currency | IModel<Currency>)` sets the decimals (2 for EUR, 0 for JPY; input is rounded half-even) and the symbol, shown before or after the amount as the locale puts it; the user may type the symbol too. `setMin`/`setMax` take `BigDecimal`s.
- `new OatPercentField(id, label, model)`: `OatPercentField`, a `BigDecimal` holding the number as shown (19 means 19%), with a `%` suffix; `setFractionDigits(n)` (default 2), `setMin`/`setMax`.
- `new OatDateRangeField(id, label, model)`: `OatDateRangeField`, a `DateRange(from, to)` (`LocalDate`s, either may be `null`; `contains(day)`) edited as two date inputs in an input group, named "From"/"To". `setRequired(true)` needs both ends; an end before the start fails with `OatDateRangeField.order`.
- `new OatAutoCompleteField<>(id, label, model)`: `OatAutoCompleteField<T>`, Wicket's `AutoCompleteTextField` with an Oat-styled list: `setChoices(text -> service.search(text))` (called as the user types; `setMaxChoices(n)`, 10 by default), `setDisplay(T::name)`. On submit the text must match a suggestion (exactly, else ignoring case) and the value is that object; otherwise `OatAutoCompleteField.noMatch`. `setFreeText(text -> value)` accepts other text. Works inside an `OatDialog`/`OatPopover` (`wicket-oat.js` lifts the list above them).
- `new OatCustomField<>(id, label, model, (id, model) -> input)`: `OatCustomField<T>`, an Oat field (legend, hint, inline errors, required mark, label from `.properties`/model from a `CompoundPropertyModel` when left out) around your own input made of several inputs, usually a `FormComponentPanel<T>`. Every form component inside gets `aria-describedby` (the hint/error) and `aria-invalid`; give each its own `aria-label`.
- `new OatTagInput(id, label, model)`: Tag/chip input bound to an `IModel<List<String>>`. Tags are trimmed and de-duplicated; no tags is an empty list (and fails `setRequired(true)`). As in Oat's widget, a comma separates tags, so a tag can't contain one. Text typed without Enter or a comma is submitted as a tag too. The label, hint/error and `setPlaceholder(...)` are on the visible text box (`"tags:taginput:text"` in tests); the tags are submitted in the hidden `getInput()` (`"tags:input"`).

- `new OatFieldset(id, legend?)`: `OatFieldset`, a titled form section. A `Border`, so it goes on a `<fieldset wicket:id="...">` whose content it wraps; `add(...)` puts components inside it, and fields there still inherit a parent `CompoundPropertyModel`. The legend is looked up by id when left out; `setDescription(text)` adds a line under it. Add `Oat.Behaviors.row()` to lay out its fields on the grid.

## Data & Feedback
- `new OatStatCard(id, label, value)`: `OatStatCard`, a `Border` (e.g. on an `<article>`) showing one key figure: label, value in large type (numbers grouped in the user's locale; pass a `String` model for amounts), and optionally `setTrend(IModel<List<Number>>)` - a sparkline under it - and `setChange(IModel<Number> percent)` - a badge such as `+12.5%`, green for a rise and red for a fall, or the other way round with `setChange(model, false)` - and `setHint(model)`, e.g. "vs. last month". Its tag's content is shown below the figure.
- `new OatDescriptionList(id, model?)`: `OatDescriptionList` on a `<dl>`: a record's fields as label/value pairs, labels beside values (stacked on narrow screens). `addProperty("customer.name")` reads a property of its model, labelled by the `.properties` entry with that key; `addItem(label, valueModel)`; `addItem(labelModel, id -> component)` for a badge or link. Numbers and dates follow the locale; an empty value shows "—".
- `new OatTimeline<>(id, eventsModel, Event::title, Event::time)`: `OatTimeline`, events in the given order along a line, each with a marker, title, time (any `java.time` value, localized, in a `<time datetime>`; `null` leaves it out) and `setDescription(fn)`; `setVariant(fn)` colors a marker (`SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `DANGER`).
- `new OatSteps(id, List<String> titles | IModel<List<String>>, IModel<Integer> current)`: `OatSteps`, numbered steps joined by a line showing where a process stands (an order from "Ordered" to "Delivered"); steps before `current` are done, `current` is highlighted (`aria-current="step"`), later ones still to come; a current index past the last marks all done, `null` none. `setOnSelect((target, index) -> ...)` makes done steps links back; `setLabel(model)` names the list (default `OatSteps.label`, "Steps"). Has a markup id for `target.add(steps)`. `OatWizard` draws its steps with it (test path `"wizard:steps:list:items:0:link"`).
- `OatFilter.onChange(id, model, choicesModel, target -> ...)` / `new OatFilter<>(id, model, choicesModel) { onChange(target) }`: `OatFilter<T>`, a row of chips choosing one value above a list or table (e.g. a status); the chosen chip is filled, and choosing one sets the model and runs `onChange` over Ajax (re-render the list there, not the filter). `setNullValid(true)` adds a first "All" chip (`OatFilter.all`, value `""`) for `null`; without it a value is required. `setChoiceRenderer(renderer)` gives the chips' text and ids (default: `toString`, with strings, numbers and enums as their own ids and other values by position; `new EnumChoiceRenderer<>(this)` for translated enums, `new ChoiceRenderer<>("name", "id")` for entities). The chips are the radio buttons of a Wicket `RadioChoice` in a `<fieldset>` named by `setLabel(model)` or the id looked up in `.properties` (falling back to the id); the arrow keys move between them. Choices are read once per request, `null` among them is left out, and a `null` model binds by the id to a parent `CompoundPropertyModel`. It has its own form, so it works anywhere, also in a page's form or an `OatDrawer`. In tests: post the chip's value for the choice's input name, `tester.getRequest().getPostParameters().setParameterValue(choice.getInputName(), "paid")`, then `executeAjaxEvent("filter:form:choice", "change")`.
- `new OatList<>(id, rowsModel, Row::title)`: `OatList`, rows as in a phone app: title, `setSubtitle(fn)` line under it, `setLeading((id, rowModel) -> component)` in front (an `OatAvatar`, `OatIcon`) and `setTrailing(...)` at the end (an `OatBadge`; a button in a `Fragment`/panel of its own, as the part's tag is a `<div>`); the factories must use the id given. `setOnClick((target, row) -> ...)` makes the title a link covering the row (buttons at the end stay clickable); it gets the row from the row's model, which finds it by position like a `ListView`'s. `setEmptyState(id -> component)` shows instead of the list while there are no rows (also for a `null` list). The rows are read once per request; `setReuseItems(true)` for form fields in the rows (the parts must then read the row through its model). On any tag; has a markup id for `target.add(list)`.
- `new OatIndicator(id, IModel<?> count)` / `OatIndicator.status(id, IModel<OatVariant>, IModel<String> label)`: `OatIndicator`, a Border putting a badge (count or short word, hidden while `null`, 0 or empty; `setVariant(OatVariant.DANGER)`) on the top-end corner, or an `OatStatus` dot on the bottom-end corner (its color from `status`'s variant; `setVariant` throws there), of what is inside its tag (`<span wicket:id="inbox"><a wicket:id="link">Inbox</a></span>`; add the content with `indicator.add(...)`). `setCorner(Corner.TOP_START|...)`. Has a markup id, so `target.add(indicator)` updates it. As a Border it needs markup inside its tag, so in a factory slot (e.g. `OatList.setLeading`) wrap it in a `Fragment`. The badge comes after the link, so a focused link's name lacks it: `link.add(AttributeModifier.replace("aria-describedby", () -> indicator.getItem().getMarkupId()))` (the item always has a markup id).
- `new OatStatus(id, IModel<OatVariant>, IModel<String> label)`: `OatStatus`, a small dot on any tag (e.g. a `<span>`) in the variant's color (primary, `SECONDARY` gray, `SUCCESS`, `WARNING`, `DANGER`); with a label it is `role="img"` with `aria-label`, without one `aria-hidden` (when text beside it says the same).
- `new OatMessageList<>(id, messages, Msg::author, Msg::text, Msg::time)`: `OatMessageList<T>`, comments or notes in order: avatar (initials of the author, or `setAvatar(m -> imageUrl)`), author, time (`java.time`, localized `<time datetime>`), escaped text keeping line breaks. Has a markup id for `target.add(list)`.
- `new OatMessageInput(id, (target, text) -> ...)`: `OatMessageInput`, a text area (named by `OatMessageInput.label`) and a Send button (busy); sends the stripped text, ignores blank ones, then empties the box.
- Data table extras: `new OatRowDetailsColumn<>((id, rowModel) -> panel)` expands a row into a full-width panel under it (created on first open, rendered on a `<div>`; expanded rows kept by `equals`, or by key with `new OatRowDetailsColumn<>(details, expandedIds, Row::getId)`; `isExpanded/setExpanded`). `new OatEditableColumn<T, S, V>(header, sort, getter, setter)` with `.setType(Integer.class)`, `.setRequired`, `.addValidator`, `.setOnSave((target, row) -> ...)`: a button that becomes a field with Save/Cancel (Enter saves, Escape cancels via `wicket-oat.js`, errors inline). On `OatDataTable`: `setColumnChooser(true)` (a "Columns" popover; `setColumnVisible(index, bool)`), `setCsvExport("file.csv")` ("Export CSV", `OatCsvExport.write(provider, columns, locale, out)`: `IExportableColumn`s with a header, plain numbers, ISO dates, CSV-injection-safe). Each row is a `<tbody class="oat-row">`; `OatDataTable.Row#getDetails()`.
- `new OatLoadMoreList<>(id, IDataProvider, batchSize, (id, itemModel) -> component)`: `OatLoadMoreList<T>`, a list (`role="list"`) showing a batch at a time; "Load more (20 of 64)" (`OatLoadMoreList.more`) appends the next one over Ajax without re-rendering the rest. `setLoadOnScroll(true)` loads as the button comes into view, including inside a scrolling pane. Call `reset(target)` after the data changes. Keeps loaded rows in the page, so it suits hundreds of items, not tens of thousands.
- Charts in `dev.jbaby.wicket.oat.components.chart`, all server-side SVG with a title (`setTitle`), hover values, a "Data" table (`OatChart.data`; `setCategoryHeader(model)` names its first column) and `setValueFormat((number, locale) -> text)`. The colors are `--oat-chart-1..8`, stepped for light and dark:
  - `new OatBarChart<>(id, items, Item::name, Item::value)`: horizontal bars, with the name before each bar and the value after it. Values ≥ 0.
  - `new OatColumnChart<>(id, items, Item::label, Item::value)`: columns for ordered categories. The highest and the last column are labelled; at most 8 x-axis labels.
  - `new OatLineChart<>(id, items, Item::label).addSeries(name, Item::value)`: up to 3 series (`MAX_SERIES`), with a legend from two on. A single series gets an area and its last value labelled; a `null` leaves a gap.
  - `new OatDonutChart<>(id, items, Item::name, Item::value)`: a ring with the total, and a legend of values and shares; above 6 parts the smallest become "Other" (`OatChart.other`). The table keeps every item.
  - `new OatSparkline(id, IModel<List<Number>>)`: a small trend line without axes (decorative, `aria-hidden`), with the latest value as a dot. `OatStatCard.setTrend(model)` adds one under the figure.
- `new OatIcon(id, name)`: `OatIcon`, inline SVG from 64 Lucide icons (`OatIcon.names()`: pencil, trash-2, plus, search, mail, ...), 1em at the text's color. On `<svg wicket:id>` or any tag (the SVG goes inside). Decorative (`aria-hidden`) unless you `setLabel(text)`; add your own with `OatIcon.register(name, "<path d=...>")`. `OatIcon.ofNullable(id, name)` is an icon, or for a `null` name a hidden placeholder for the markup's tag.
- `new OatCookieConsent(id)`: `OatCookieConsent`, a card fixed at the bottom with Accept / Only necessary (`OatCookieConsent.*` texts); `setPolicyLink(PageClass)`, `setOnAnswer(accepted -> ...)`. The answer is stored for a year in the `oat-cookie-consent` cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite Lax). Check it with `OatCookieConsent.isAccepted()` / `isAnswered()`.
- `OatLazyLoadPanel.of(id, id -> component)`: `OatLazyLoadPanel`, Wicket's `AjaxLazyLoadPanel` with Oat skeletons (3 lines by default; `setPlaceholder(Shape, count)`) while the content loads over Ajax right after the page (0.1 s). Subclass it to override `isContentReady()` and wait for background work, polled every `getUpdateInterval()` (1 s, as in Wicket; the page's lazy panels share one timer at the shortest interval of those still waiting, so don't make it short).
- `new OatFeedbackPanel(id, filter?)`: `OatFeedbackPanel`, a Wicket `FeedbackPanel` rendering each `info()`/`success()`/`warn()`/`error()` message as an Oat alert of the matching variant. It adds itself to Ajax responses when it has messages to show or clear, so no `target.add(feedback)` is needed. By default it leaves out errors Oat form fields already show inline (`NotShownInlineFilter`); pass `(IFeedbackMessageFilter) null` to show everything. `new OatFeedbackPanel(id, fence, filter?)` shows only the messages of `fence` (e.g. a form) and the components in it, as Wicket's `FencedFeedbackPanel` (which it extends); a panel without a fence and `feedbackToasts()` then leave those out, even one with a filter: to show one component's messages inside a fence, fence it (`new OatFeedbackPanel(id, component)`) rather than filtering by it. A panel without messages takes no space.
- `new OatDataTable<>(id, columns, dataProvider, rowsPerPage)`: `OatDataTable`, a styled Wicket DataTable, paged with `OatAjaxPagingNavigator`; sortable headers show an arrow and set `aria-sort`; sorting and paging re-render the table over Ajax (plain links without JavaScript). It has a markup id (`target.add(table)`; `getTable()` is the inner `DataTable`), and is pageable itself (`IPageableItems`: `setCurrentPage`, `getPageCount`, `setItemsPerPage`; `addTopToolbar` (below the column headers)/`addBottomToolbar`). Use `setEmptyState(id -> emptyState(id, "No results"))` for a custom placeholder when it has no rows, and `setToolbar(id -> component)` for a toolbar above it (e.g. a search form; in its Ajax handler `table.setCurrentPage(0); target.add(table.getTable())`); both factories must use the id they are given. With an `OatSelectionColumn`, `addBulkAction(label, (target, rows) -> ...)` / `addBulkAction(IModel label, OatVariant, ...)` add buttons to a bar shown while rows are selected ("3 selected", the actions, "Clear selection"); actions get a copy of the selected rows and should call `clearSelection(target)` when done.
- Columns in `dev.jbaby.wicket.oat.components.table` (all take a header model, an optional sort property and a lambda for the value):
  - `OatLinkColumn.toPage(header, sort, label, PageClass, row -> pageParameters)` / `OatLinkColumn.onClick(header, sort, label, (target, row) -> ...)`.
  - `new OatBadgeColumn<>(header, sort, value, row -> OatVariant)`: the value as a badge colored per row, e.g. a status.
  - `new OatNumberColumn<>(header, sort, value)`: locale-formatted and right-aligned; `.setFractionDigits(min, max)`, `.setCurrency(Currency)` or `.setCurrency(Row::currency)` for amounts.
  - `new OatDateColumn<>(header, sort, value)`: any `java.time` value in the locale's style (dates `MEDIUM`, times `SHORT`); `.setStyle(date, time)`, `.setPattern("yyyy-MM-dd")`, `.setZone(zone)` for `Instant`s. A `LONG`/`FULL` time style shows the zone (an `OffsetDateTime`'s offset); a `LocalDateTime` or `LocalTime` shows `MEDIUM` instead. A `YearMonth` or other value without a date or time of day shows its `toString()` unless a pattern is set.
  - `new OatBooleanColumn<>(header, sort, value)`: a read-only checkbox named after the column.
  - `new OatActionsColumn<>()`: a "⋯" menu per row; `addAction(label, (target, row) -> ...)` returns the action for `.setVariant(OatVariant.DANGER)` (shown in red) and `.setVisibleWhen(row -> ...)`. A row without visible actions shows no button. `setVisibleWhen` is checked again on click (an action the row no longer shows doesn't run; its menu re-renders), which needs a row model that reloads the row, e.g. a `LoadableDetachableModel` from the provider, not `Model.of(row)`.
  - `new OatSelectionColumn<>(IModel<? extends Collection<T>> selection)`: row checkboxes plus a "select all on this page" box in the header; kept across pages and sorting, compared with `equals`. For entities, select by key so the page keeps only ids, and load the rows by key: `new OatSelectionColumn<>(IModel<Set<Long>> selectedIds, Invoice::getId, ids -> invoices.findAllById(ids))` (any `Iterable`); `getSelectedRows(provider)` (and bulk actions) then get every selected row, also those a search hides. Without the loader they are looked up through the data provider, which reads every row and misses those it doesn't return at the time. Sends `OatSelectionColumn.SelectionChanged` (bubbling) on every change.
- `new OatProgress(id, value, max?)`: Standard `<progress>` bar; `max` is an optional bound model.
- `new OatRadialProgress(id, value | IModel<? extends Number> value, IModel<? extends Number> max?)`: `OatRadialProgress`, a ring filling clockwise with the percentage in the middle (rounded down); `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuemax`/`aria-valuetext`, so name it in the markup (`<div wicket:id="storage" aria-label="Storage used">`). `setVariant(OatVariant | IModel<OatVariant>)` colors the ring, `setText(model)` replaces the percentage (e.g. "3/5"); a `null` value leaves it empty. 4rem wide (`--oat-radial-progress-size`); has a markup id. On any tag.
- `new OatRating(id, Number | IModel<? extends Number>)`: `OatRating`, a read-only rating as stars, rounded to half a star, `role="img"` named "4.5 out of 5 stars" (`OatRating.label`; `null` is `OatRating.none`, "Not rated yet"). As tall as the surrounding text; `setMax(1..10)`. On any tag, e.g. a `<span>`. Colors: `--oat-rating-color` (amber), `--oat-rating-empty`.
- `new OatMeter(id, value)`: Simple `<meter>`.
- `new OatMeter(id, value, min, max, low, high, optimum)`: Advanced `<meter>` with full range/zone control.
- `new OatSpinner(id, size?)`: Loading indicator.
- CSS only, from `wicket-oat.css`: `<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>` is styled as a key (a `<kbd>` holding `<kbd>`s, a whole shortcut, is not); `<div class="oat-divider">or</div>` is a line across with the word in the middle, an empty one just the line.
- `new OatSkeleton(id, shape?)`: Placeholder for loading content.

## Usage Example
```java
add(OatButton.onClick("myBtn", "Save", target -> {
    // Save logic
    Oat.toast(target, "Saved!", OatVariant.SUCCESS);
}));
```

Source: https://github.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/blob/v0.6.0/wicket-oat/references/behaviors.md

# Wicket Oat Behaviors

Use `Oat.Behaviors` for the "Power Path" to style existing Wicket components via composition.

## Available Behaviors
- `accordion(exclusive?)`: Turns a container into an accordion.
- `ajaxBusy()`: While an Ajax link/button's request runs, sets `aria-busy="true"` (Oat's spinner) and drops further clicks, so it can't run twice. `OatButton`, `OatSubmitButton` and `OatDialog` (its confirm button) turn it on with `setBusyIndicator(true)`; it's off by default. Needs `WicketOats.install`.
- `alert(variant?)`: Applies alert styling and `role="alert"`.
- `badge(variant?)`: Applies badge styling.
- `button()`: Styles any component (Link, Button, etc.) as an Oat button.
- `buttonGroup()`: Styles a container as a button group.
- `card()`: Styles a container as a card.
- `contextMenu()`: `ContextMenuBehavior`, a menu of actions opened by right-click, Shift+F10 or the Menu key on the component. `addAction(label, target -> ...)`, `addAction(IModel label, OatVariant.DANGER, ...)`. It's keyboard navigable and returns focus to the component when it closes. Works inside an `OatDialog`, `OatDrawer` or `OatPopover`. Uses `wicket-oat.js` (CSP-safe).
- `field()`: Styles a form field container.
- `hint()`: Styles a small text hint inside a field.
- `inputGroup()`: Joins a `<fieldset>`'s inputs, buttons and `<label>`/`<legend>` addons into one control (`class="group"`). Oat fields have `setPrefix`/`setSuffix` for this.
- `row()`, `col(span)`, `col(span, offset)`, `container()`: Oat's 12-column grid (`row`, `col-1`...`col-12`, `offset-1`...`offset-6`, `container`); it drops to one column on narrow screens. On an Oat form field they apply to the field's own tag.
- `hstack()` / `vstack()`: A wrapping row or a column with Oat's standard gap.
- `oatSwitch()`: Turns a `CheckBox` into a visual toggle switch.
- `tooltip(text)`: Adds a styled tooltip.
- `spinner(size?)`: Adds a spinner overlay/logic.
- `skeleton(shape?)`: Adds a skeleton loading effect.
- `theme()`: Allows programmatic theme application to a component.
- `density()` / `density(OatDensity)`: Applies the configured or a given density (`data-density`), e.g. a compact table, or `DEFAULT` spacing for one part of a compact app.
- `clientSideClick(javascript)`: Efficiently runs JS on click while maintaining CSP.
- `feedbackToasts(filter?)`: Add to a page (or base page) to show `info()`/`success()`/`warn()`/`error()` feedback messages - including session messages - as Oat toasts, on full renders and during Ajax requests without touching the `AjaxRequestTarget`. By default leaves out errors Oat form fields already show inline, and the messages of a container that an `OatFeedbackPanel` with a fence shows.

## Composition Example
```java
// Style a standard Wicket AjaxLink as a primary Oat button (the default variant)
add(new AjaxLink<Void>("id") {
    @Override
    public void onClick(AjaxRequestTarget target) { ... }
}.add(Oat.Behaviors.button()));
```

---

Source: https://github.com/danielbartl/wicket-oat/blob/v0.6.0/wicket-oat/references/theming.md

# Wicket Oat Theming

Theming is controlled by the `data-theme` attribute, which `OatAppLayout` sets on `<html>` from the current user's theme. There is no special session class: the choice is kept by an `OatThemeStore` - by default `CookieThemeStore` (an `oat-theme` cookie kept for a year, cached in the session).

## Built-in Themes
`OatTheme` constants: `LIGHT`, `DARK`, `MIDNIGHT`, `NORD`, `EVERFOREST`, `TOKYO_NIGHT`, `ROSE_PINE_DAWN`, `ROYAL`, `CLAY`, `CATPPUCCIN_MOCHA`, `CATPPUCCIN_LATTE`, `MATERIAL`, `DAISY`, `ULTRAVIOLET`, `HALLOWEEN`, `XMAS`, `WIREFRAME`, `BUSINESS`, `BUSINESS_DARK` (a sober light/dark pair for business apps). `OatTheme` is a record (`value`, `label`, `icon`); `OatTheme.builtIns()` lists them.

## Configuring
`WicketOats.install(app)` returns the application's `OatSettings`:

```java
WicketOats.install(this)
        .setDefaultTheme(OatTheme.LIGHT)                 // DARK by default; null follows the browser
        .addTheme(new OatTheme("custom-blue", "Custom Blue", "🔵"))
        .setThemeStore(new SessionThemeStore());         // optional: session only, no cookie
```

`setThemes(List.of(...))` limits which themes users can pick. `OatSettings.get()` returns the settings during a request.

## Changing Themes
```java
OatTheme.setCurrent(OatTheme.NORD);   // for the current user; null goes back to the default
OatTheme theme = OatTheme.current();  // the stored choice if registered, else the default (may be null)
```

`new OatThemeSwitcher("id")` renders a link per registered theme (icon, or label if none), marking the current one with `aria-current="true"`.

## Applying a Theme
- `OatAppLayout` applies the current theme to `<html>` automatically.
- With your own base page: `add(new OatHtml("html"))` on `<html wicket:id="html">`. It sets `data-theme`, `data-density` and `lang`, like the layouts, and is transparent, so the page's components can sit anywhere inside it.
- `Oat.Behaviors.theme(OatTheme.LIGHT)` pins one component to a theme, whatever the user chose.

## Density
Independent of the theme: `OatSettings.setDensity(OatDensity.COMPACT)` tightens spacing and body text app-wide (`DEFAULT` otherwise). `OatAppLayout` sets it as `data-density` on `<html>`; with your own base page the `OatHtml` on `<html>` sets it. `Oat.Behaviors.density(OatDensity.COMPACT)` makes one component compact, e.g. a large table; `Oat.Behaviors.density(OatDensity.DEFAULT)` keeps one part at Oat's own spacing in a compact app.

## Custom Themes
Define the CSS variables, then register the theme so it can be chosen:

```css
[data-theme="custom-blue"] {
    color-scheme: dark;
    --background: #001f3f;
    --foreground: #ffffff;
    --card: #00264d;
    --primary: #0074d9;
    --border: #003366;
}
```

Theme values must be lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Only registered themes are accepted from the cookie; an unknown value falls back to the default.
